messages:
elaine: heads up — after the canary deploy I bumped into a p95/p99 spike for SSE streams that include tool-calls. CI perf also flagged +28% on stream_latency_512. canary rollout paused. :eyes:
michael: seeing identical in prod canary. small event chunks are not reaching clients until a bigger flush — UI shows nothing for ~200-400ms then a big chunk. suspect flush behavior change in last PR.
deploy-bot: deploy completed: commit abcd123 (PR #4623) 'toolcall: compact framing and header refactor' -> canary slot
sam: ran a quick flamegraph on the slow traces. proto.Serialize/Encode went from ~12% to ~45% of CPU in the tail for these streams. lots of memcpy hotspots.
jia: also noticed kernel-autoselect telemetry shifted a bit — more fallbacks to the generic encode path when payloads >2kB after that PR. could be correlated.
tyler: starting a bisect between 4620..4630 now. suspect #4623 as the main delta. I'll try a revert in canary first.
michael: note: KV cache payloads grew a bit due to bundled prefixes (recent optimize change) — that increases toolcall body size so maybe hitting different path.
sam: quick trace snippet I captured:
```
# simplified trace for a single streaming event
proto.Serialize(toolcall_msg) -> memcpy(header) -> memcpy(body) -> memcpy(checksum)
writev([hdr, body]) # previously we ensured an immediate flush after header
# after #4623: we build a single buffer and rely on socket coalescing, no explicit small-write flush
```
this means small SSE writes are being combined and not flushed, which clients then render late.
chelsea: CI regression: tools/ci/perf/stream_latency_512 shows p99 increased from ~210ms -> ~410ms on canary. we held the rollout at 60% because of the alert. blocking release.
tyler: revert applied to canary (reverted PR #4623). rerunning perf now.
replay-bot: perf bench run 2130456820: stream_latency_512 -> p50: 45ms, p95: 150ms, p99: 230ms (after revert). prior to revert on canary p99 was 410ms.
elaine: revert recovered most of the tail. good. but we still need a proper fix that doesn't regress proto.Serialize nor change SSE flush semantics. :thumbsup:
jia: plan: I'll open a follow-up PR to restore an explicit small-write flush for SSE events (MSG_MORE/MSG_EOR or socket-level flush) and add a microbenchmark for proto.Serialize to CI. also add a test that simulates small streaming writes to catch this.
sam: will dig into the serialization path; there's an extra header copy introduced when we compacted framing. maybe we can build header in-place or use zero-copy slices to drop the extra memcpy. I'll prototype.
tyler: filing a rollout-blocker issue and adding to release board. keeping rollout paused until patch lands + perf CI green.
elaine: assign sam + jia. please post progress here. if any customer incidents surface we may schedule a brief postmortem. ops-bot: notified SRE oncall. :warning:
